experiment: E40 two-gate attack-aware rejection on the frozen E36 WCCN model
motivation: E36C outer macro ASafeR=0.6818 at RA=0.0609: attacked trials are neither identified correctly nor rejected, and rejection counts as safe. A second rejection gate based on the maximum cosine, which measures how far the winning prototype is from the sample, rejects attacked trials that the distance_ratio gate lets through. U is preserved because the distance_ratio gate is retained.

data.source: Train session1 only; read-only reuse of the E36 feature cache and Train MAT files

model.identity_model: frozen E36 detrend_zband_cov5_wccn_prototype at the E36 selected shrinkage and eigenvalue floor
model.training: none; E40 changes only the inference-time rejection rule

rule.threshold_solving: shared lower quantile q over 200 evenly spaced values in [0.001, 0.05] of the pooled inner clean-known arrays; t_dr = quantile(distance_ratio, q), t_mc = quantile(max_cosine, q); choose q whose joint clean-known acceptance is closest to 0.95
rule.rationale: the two statistics are positively correlated, so a shared lower quantile near 0.02 yields about 95% joint clean acceptance; solving on clean known only keeps the operating point fixed at the E36 95% acceptance budget for C/U comparability
rule.development_note: the two-gate form and the choice of max_cosine as the second statistic were developed on outer fold 1 inner fold 1 only, from a candidate list that also included whitened feature energy, whitened-prototype distance, spectral flatness, high-band power ratio, and random-smoothing flip rates at sigma 0.005/0.01/0.02/0.05/0.10/0.20. Random-smoothing flips, spectral flatness and high-band ratio were rejected as near-chance. No outer fold beyond fold 1 and no Test data were used for this choice.

ablations.confidence_only: accept iff distance_ratio >= its own inner clean-known q05; this reproduces the E36C operating point on the same folds and separates the gain of the second gate from the gain of the fold protocol

evaluation.inner_folds: E36 five outer groups x two inner folds, identical seeds and continuous trial blocks
evaluation.subset: E36 stratified first 8 trials per identity/task by trial/path for clean known and pseudo-unknown, identical to E36C
evaluation.aggregation: each inner run is scored in its own enrolled label space (the two inner runs of an outer fold exclude different pseudo-unknown subjects, so their class axes differ and must not be concatenated); the two inner runs are averaged, then the five outer folds are averaged
evaluation.detector_audit: AUROC and best F1 of -max_cosine as an attacked-versus-clean-known classifier on the same pooled trials; reported as a detector audit, never used to choose thresholds
evaluation.rej_definition: mean adversarial rejection rate, i.e. 1 - accepted fraction of attacked known trials

targets.success: strict improvement over both the internal confidence_only ablation and the E36C outer reference on macro ASafeR, macro A and macro Score, with C>=0.95, U>=0.95 and no loss of identity F1
targets.RA_note: macro RA>=0.95 remains the stated E36 gate but is not reachable at SNR20 with this frozen model; E40 does not claim it

reporting.evidence_boundary: Train-only pseudo-unknown, E36 continuous file-block proxy, attack subsets that overlap the fit split exactly as in E36C, and a rule developed on one inner fold; this is a mechanism comparison, not untouched validation and not a Test or cross-session claim
